A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProbeSDF and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material. Content can be reliably matched across renumbering and rearrangement.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, image-quality, timing, and ablation results on MVMannequins, ActorsHQ, DTU, and BlendedMVS, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds quantitative MVMannequins ablations in Table 5.

M1.justification: The decoupled spatial/probe representation, spherical harmonics, Fresnel inputs, small MLP, SDF rendering, and core losses remain unchanged. Additional scheduling and gradient-weighting descriptions document implementation details without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same reconstruction tasks on MVMannequins, ActorsHQ, DTU, and BlendedMVS, retaining the same scene coverage. The added component ablations reuse existing data.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same baseline sets: MMH, Voxurf, NeuS2, COLMAP, and 2DGS on MVMannequins; Voxurf and NeuS2 on ActorsHQ and BlendedMVS; and Voxurf, NeuS2, and 2DGS on DTU. RealityCapture comparisons displayed in v2's main text already appeared in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: v2 Table 5 introduces controls without probe smoothing and with the incidence-angle input fixed during training to disable Fresnel dependence. Existing benchmark settings remain consistent; newly specified grid resolutions, silhouette PSNR, and ActorsHQ rendering upscaling clarify previously reported experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative tests of probe smoothing and training without Fresnel dependence. Existing feature/order and timing analyses remain, but the joint-component visual ablation shrinks from eight configurations to four (v1 Figure 6 versus v2 Figure 8), and the BlendedMVS example is omitted from the Fresnel visual comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or run-level uncertainty. The retained averages summarize scenes rather than repeated trials.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark and detailed appendix tables retain identical values. New Table 5 reports Chamfer/PSNR of 1.09 mm/36.91 dB without probe smoothing and 1.18 mm/36.79 dB without Fresnel dependence, versus 1.04 mm/36.81 dB for the full model. v2 also omits v1's explicit above-100-Hz ActorsHQ rendering result.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3.2 explicitly gives derivatives of angular features with respect to probe coefficients and reflected direction in equations 8–9. v2 removes these equations and the accompanying linearity/backpropagation explanation without relocating them to the appendix. The remaining mathematical formulation is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: decoupled appearance encoding enables a small decoder, fast training, real-time rendering, and competitive reconstruction quality across four datasets.

C2.justification: v2 Section 6 explicitly states that relighting and material editing are unsupported, while suggesting probe fine-tuning for new lighting as future work. Existing limitations concerning extrapolation and shape-radiance ambiguity remain.

D1.justification: v1 provides a general Adam/coarse-to-fine description; v2 adds Appendix A and Tables 7–10 with dataset-specific learning rates, loss weights, iteration counts, and batch schedules, plus optimizer coefficients, warm-up, and initialization details. It also specifies grid resolutions and evaluation details, discloses additional gradient reweighting, and supplies a source-code URL.

R1.justification: v2 adds PGSR, Fast Dipole Sums, Sur2f, and Objects as Volumes. Related work briefly broadens the positioning toward point-based and hybrid representations that might benefit from the appearance model, while retaining the original research framing.

P1.justification: v2 condenses and edits related work, introduces explicit Protocol and Ablations paragraphs, refines the conclusion and terminology, and changes supplementary headings from numbered sections to letters. The overall narrative and main section order remain stable.

P2.justification: The main experimental presentation is substantially reassembled. v2 Figures 5–7 reuse appendix comparisons with reference columns, labels, and close-ups; Figures 8–9 reorganize visual ablations and introduce difference maps. Tables are rearranged, and five additional tables present the new ablation and four training schedules.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through detailed training schedules, clearer evaluation documentation, and code-access information. Table 5 adds useful quantitative checks of two components. These gains outweigh the limited loss of explicit gradient derivations and some visual ablation combinations, but the core method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged, making the overall improvement incremental.
